name: Iron Ingot
description: Bog-iron smelted at Merrowby's red-door forge. Vale smiths stamp the flat with a small bell so the metal knows where it came from.

name: Ash Wood
description: A straight length of seasoned ash. Vale bowyers cut a stave on a Tollday and do not speak of it until it is strung.

name: Oak Plank
description: Hedgerow oak, sawn and dried. Hearthvale grows its oaks in hedges rather than woods, so every plank has a bend where it leaned toward the road.

name: Leather
description: Oak-bark cured hide from the Fernhold lodges. It smells of the Briarwold for a year.

name: Chalk
description: White chalk from the Downs. The Chalk Hound is cut from this, and so are the tally-marks on a Warden's door.

name: Flint
description: Black flint from a chalk seam. It strikes sparks, and it is the oldest tool in the Vale, older than the Toll.

name: Linen
description: Woven flax from the Brightwater quays, bleached white on the shingle under the Lamp.

name: Wool
description: Skerrow fleece, carded and spun. The clans knit while they remember; they say it is the same work.

name: Bell-Bronze Scrap
description: A shard of Oroth bell-metal. Held against the teeth it still hums. Smiths who work it say it wants a note back.

name: Kingbone
description: A section of the Stone-Thrall King's bone: giant-bone that stood up and walked again in Oskeld's singing shaft. Clan-smiths will not touch it without first saying its name.

name: Silver Ore
description: Brindlecrag silver, veined through limestone. The miners say the vein follows a giant's arm down into the dark.

name: Giant-Bone Shard
description: Bone from the Skerrow scree, left when the giants were breathed back in and their weight was not. It takes an edge like stone and a polish like horn.

name: Indigo Dye
description: Marsh indigo from Sedgemire, the only blue in Wickmere. Reedfolk dye the lanterns of their dead with it.

name: Wolf Pelt
description: The grey-gold pelt of a down wolf. Fernhold pays for them; Merrowby's children wear them on Candle Night.

name: Bristleback Tusk
description: A curved tusk from a bristleback. Vale hunters hang one over the door so the next boar knows.

name: Ember Mote
description: A spark of a foe's last warmth, caught by a Kindling word before it went quiet. It hovers a finger's breadth above the palm. Name-tables burn these to write a note into iron.
